product: VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 - VCF Automation (successor to vRealize / Aria Automation)

source.statement: THIS CONTRACT IS DERIVED FROM REFERENCE DOCUMENTATION, NOT FROM A PUBLISHED SPECIFICATION. VCF Automation has no OpenAPI/Swagger specification in the vmware/vcf-api-specs (Apache-2.0) repository. Every path, query parameter, field, required/optional split, status code and enum value below was transcribed by hand from the xAPIs reference pages on developer.broadcom.com that are recorded, with their fetch dates, in docs/official_sources.json. It is a faithful transcription of prose reference material and not a machine-readable artifact published by the vendor; where the reference is silent this contract states an explicit local decision under the key 'local_decision' rather than presenting the choice as vendor-documented.

api_version.rule: Every request in this contract MUST carry apiVersion=2021-07-15 in the query string. The reference marks apiVersion Required on PATCH /iaas/api/cloud-accounts/{id} and Optional elsewhere; this contract requires it everywhere so that a rotation cannot straddle two server-selected API versions.
api_version.local_decision: Pinning one version for all five operations is a contract-level decision. The reference documents the yyyy-MM-dd convention and uses 2021-07-15 in its examples; it does not mandate a single version across a call sequence.

auth.rule: Every request in this contract MUST carry the Authorization header. The access token is obtained out of band and is NOT part of this contract; no token-issuing operation is included here.
auth.note: The bearer token is an identity credential for the caller. It is unrelated to the cloud account's privateKeyId/privateKey, which are the credentials this contract rotates.

query_parameters.name: $select
query_parameters.description: Subset of properties to include in the response.

202.description: The update was accepted and is tracked asynchronously. The rotation is NOT complete when this returns.

query_parameters.name: periodicHealthCheckId
query_parameters.description: Identifies a scheduled health check as opposed to a manually initiated one. Omit for a manual check.

closed_operation_set.rule: The five operations above are the entire contract. Any other method+path pair is out of contract; a conforming client never issues one.

UpdateCloudAccountSpecification.description: Request body of Update Cloud Account Async. Field names, types and the required/optional split are transcribed from the reference data-structure page.

name.description: A human-friendly name used as an identifier in APIs that support this option.

cloudAccountProperties.description: Cloud Account specific properties supplied in as name value pairs.

regions.description: A set of regions to enable provisioning on.

privateKeyId.description: Access key id or username to be used to authenticate with the cloud account.

privateKey.description: Secret access key or password to be used to authenticate with the cloud account.

customProperties.description: Additional custom properties that may be used to extend the Cloud Account.

associatedCloudAccountIds.description: Cloud accounts to associate with this cloud account.

createDefaultZones.description: Create default zones for the enabled regions.

tags.description: A set of tag keys and optional values to set on the Cloud Account.

certificateInfo.description: Specification for certificate for a cloud account.

RegionSpecification.description: A region entry inside UpdateCloudAccountSpecification.regions. Carries exactly these two fields; both required.

externalRegionId.description: Unique identifier of region on the provider side.

name.description: Name of region on the provider side. In vSphere, the name of the region is different from its id.

CloudAccount.note: CloudAccount never echoes privateKey. It does not carry a 'regions' field either - the enabled regions are reported as 'enabledRegions', an array of Region.

RequestTracker.description: 202 response of the async operations and 200 response of Get Request Tracker.

omit_unset_optionals.rule: An optional field that the caller did not set MUST be absent from the serialized JSON body. It MUST NOT be emitted as null, as an empty string, as an empty array or as an empty object. This matches how the VMware.Sdk.Vcf PowerCLI model builders (the Initialize-Vcf* cmdlets) serialize their models: unset optional properties simply do not appear in ToJson() output.
omit_unset_optionals.rationale: PATCH on this API is a partial update. An explicitly-present empty value is a request to clear the field, which is materially different from not mentioning it. Sending description:"" or tags:[] during a credential rotation would silently wipe operator-set metadata off the cloud account.

required_fields_always_present.rule: name, cloudAccountProperties and regions MUST be present in every Update Cloud Account Async body, even when the rotation only intends to change the secret.
required_fields_always_present.rationale: The reference marks all three Required. Because PATCH replaces the fields it is given, name and cloudAccountProperties must be carried forward unchanged from Get Cloud Account, and regions must be reconstructed from the account's current enabledRegions, or the rotation will damage the account while changing its password.

region_projection.rule: regions in the request body is built from CloudAccount.enabledRegions by projecting each Region down to exactly {externalRegionId, name}. No other Region field (id, cloudAccountId, _links, orgId, owner, ownerType, createdAt, updatedAt) may appear in a region entry.
region_projection.rationale: enabledRegions is an array of Region; regions is an array of RegionSpecification. They are different types and the response type is not accepted verbatim as the request type.

secret_placement.rule: The new secret is transmitted only as the privateKey field of the Update Cloud Account Async JSON body. It MUST NOT appear in any URL, query string, or request header, and MUST NOT be sent on any other operation in this contract.
secret_placement.rationale: URLs and headers are routinely logged in full by proxies and by the platform's own audit trail.

async_completion.rule: Update Cloud Account Async and Run Endpoint Health Check return 202 with a RequestTracker whose status is INPROGRESS. The operation is complete only once Get Request Tracker reports a terminal status. FINISHED and FAILED are terminal; INPROGRESS is not. A 202 alone MUST NOT be treated as success.

drain_before_rotate.rule: Before issuing Update Cloud Account Async, the client MUST observe, via Get Request Trackers, that no request tracker is left in INPROGRESS. Any tracker found INPROGRESS must be followed to a terminal status first; only then may the PATCH be sent.
drain_before_rotate.rationale: This is the whole point of the scenario. A request that is already in flight was admitted under the old secret and will continue to authenticate against the provider with it. Rotating while such a request is outstanding strands it: it holds a credential the platform has already replaced, and it fails part-way through with no clean rollback. Draining first costs a few seconds and makes the rotation safe.
drain_before_rotate.ordering_requirement: In the server's request log, the last observation of every pre-existing tracker must show a terminal status and must precede the PATCH.
